title: The sheaf of lattices is a separated étale scheme
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and its topological valuation ring $A=\cO_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use universes containing the schemes, coefficient rings and the set of lattices below [def-weil-size-convention]. On the small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], $E_X$ and $A_X$ are the pullbacks of the condensed topological rings $E$ and $A$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]; modules are module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Here lisse means pro-étale locally free of finite rank, and a lattice is an embedded lisse $A_X$-module whose localization at $\ell$ is the ambient rational module. Constant sheaf means sheafification of the constant presheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. A scheme is qcqs if its underlying space is quasi-compact and its diagonal is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Separated and étale have the meanings of [def-weil-proper-morphism] and [def-weil-etale-morphism].

Let $X$ be a qcqs scheme and $L$ a lisse $E_X$-module of constant rank $r$. Let $\mathcal{L}\mathit{at}$
be the sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with $\mathcal{L}\mathit{at}(U)$ the set of lisse
$\cO_{E,U}$-submodules $M\subseteq L|_U$ with $M[1/\ell]=L|_U$.

1. If $L|_V\cong E_V^r$ on $V$, then $\mathcal{L}\mathit{at}|_V$ is the constant sheaf on the discrete set
   $\GL_r(E)/\GL_r(\cO_E)$ of $\cO_E$-lattices in $E^r$.
2. $\mathcal{L}\mathit{at}$ is represented by a separated étale $X$-scheme $\mathrm{Lat}(L)\to X$, which is
   surjective.
3. There is a universal lattice $M^{\mathrm{univ}}\subseteq q^*L$ on $\mathrm{Lat}(L)$,
   $q\colon\mathrm{Lat}(L)\to X$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations], identify the pulled-back coefficients with the continuous-function coefficient sheaves, compatibly with $A\to E$. The total-disconnectedness hypothesis holds: nonarchimedean clopen balls separate distinct points of $E$, and $A$ has the subspace topology. Module actions and inclusions transport along these ring isomorphisms. By [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell], $A_X[1/\ell]=E_X$. On module sections the localization/tensor comparison is $m/\ell^n\mapsto\ell^{-n}\otimes m$, with inverse $a/\ell^n\otimes m\mapsto am/\ell^n$, interpreted locally when necessary. Thus the lattice condition is exactly the scalar-extension condition in the lattice-classification node.

An object $(M,\alpha)$ in [lem-weil-pbc-lattice-sheaf-locally-constant] embeds in $L$ by $m\mapsto\alpha(1\otimes m)$. On free charts this is injective because $A\hookrightarrow E$ induces an injective map of continuous-function sheaves. Its image is an embedded lisse lattice. Conversely an embedded lattice gives such a pair by its scalar-extension isomorphism. Two pairs have the same image exactly when their unique isomorphism over that image intertwines $\alpha$. These constructions commute with restriction. Therefore that node's sheaf is precisely $\mathcal{L}\mathit{at}$. Its trivial-bundle classification gives clause (1), including the specified coset $g\operatorname{GL}_r(A)$ corresponding to $gA^r$.

Choose a finite affine open cover of the quasi-compact $X$. Over each member, the covering condition in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] extracts finitely many affine pieces of a trivializing pro-étale covering of $L$, whose images cover that member. Put $V$ equal to their finite disjoint union and $p:V\to X$ the induced map; on all pieces choose rank-$r$ trivializations, giving $L|_V\cong E_V^r$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], $V$ is affine; by [sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability], $p$ is weakly étale, hence flat. The images cover $X$, so $p$ is surjective. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], $p$ is quasi-compact since $X$ is quasi-separated. For every affine open $B\subset X$, its inverse image is quasi-compact and hence covered by finitely many affine opens; their images cover $B$. This verifies that $\{p\}$ is an fpqc and pro-étale covering. The pieces $V_i$ are affine pro-étale objects over $X$, not necessarily Zariski open subschemes of $X$.

source.place: (2), choose finitely many affine trivializing pro-étale charts

proof.text: Write $S=\operatorname{GL}_r(E)/\operatorname{GL}_r(A)$ and form $T=\coprod_{s\in S}V$ using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. By [lem-galois-coproduct-copies-morphisms-clopen], $V$-morphisms $W\to T$ are exactly locally constant maps $|W|\to S$. This presheaf is a sheaf for pro-étale coverings by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent]. The constant-presheaf map sends $s$ to the corresponding component section. Every morphism $W\to T$ is such a section on each of its open-and-closed inverse images of the components. Consequently its sheafification is exactly this presheaf: extend maps out of the constant presheaf by sheaf gluing on these open pieces, uniquely. Thus $T$ represents $\underline S_V$, and by step 2 represents $\mathcal{L}\mathit{at}|_V$.

source.place: (2), disjoint unions representing the locally constant lattice sheaf

proof.text: On $R=V\times_XV$, the two trivializations identify the two pullbacks of $\mathcal{L}\mathit{at}$ with $\underline S_R$. For a fixed source label $s$, their transition sends the constant section $s$ to a section of $\underline S_R$, hence by step 4 to a clopen decomposition of $R$ indexed by target labels. By [lem-galois-coproduct-copies-morphisms-clopen], this gives a morphism from that copy of $R$ to $\coprod_S R$. The coproduct universal property assembles these component maps. Applying the inverse sheaf transition gives its inverse. On a triple overlap both composites induce the same sheaf transition; the same clopen descriptions make the scheme maps equal. Hence this is a scheme descent datum on $T/V$ over $V/X$. No continuity assertion about a varying infinite permutation is required beyond its effect on each fixed label.

source.place: (2), locally constant transition action and cocycle

proof.text: Check the exact effectivity hypothesis of [lem-a1-ind-quasi-affine-fpqc-effective-descent]. For any affine open $B\subset V$ and quasi-compact open $K\subset T\times_V B=\coprod_S B$, finitely many components contain $K$: the intersections with components are an open covering of $K$. Thus $K$ is an open subscheme of a finite disjoint union of copies of $B$, which is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. More precisely $K\to B$ is quasi-affine: over any affine open $B'\subset B$, its inverse image $K'$ is the intersection of $K$ with the corresponding finite disjoint union $D'$ of copies of $B'$, again affine. It is open in $D'$, and quasi-compact because $K$ and $D'$ are quasi-compact opens of the affine, hence quasi-separated, finite union of copies of $B$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. So $K'$ is a quasi-affine scheme. The datum of step 5 therefore satisfies every hypothesis of the cited singleton-fpqc effectivity theorem (Stacks Tag 0APK). Obtain an $X$-scheme $Y$ and $Y\times_XV\cong T$ inducing that datum. No quasi-compactness of $T\to V$ is used.

The morphism $T\to V$ is étale, since on each component it is the identity and the affine-ring definition is local on the source. Its diagonal is a closed immersion: $T\times_VT$ is covered by the pairwise components $V$ indexed by $(s,t)$; the diagonal is the identity on $s=t$ and empty on $s\ne t$, so its complement is the open union of the off-diagonal components. Thus it is separated. Apply [lem-galois-fpqc-descend-etale] and [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-separated] to $p:V\to X$ to conclude that $q:Y\to X$ is étale and separated. For each $x\in X$, choose $v\in V$ above it and the point in the copy of $V$ indexed by the standard lattice $A^r$ above $v$. Its image in $Y$ lies over $x$; hence $q$ is surjective.

source.place: (2), separated and étale descent, Tags 02KU and 02VN; surjectivity

proof.text: For any $U\to X$ in $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$, set $U_V=U\times_XV$. This is an fpqc covering of $U$ by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change], and weakly étale by [sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability], hence a pro-étale covering. A section of $\mathcal{L}\mathit{at}(U)$ gives on $U_V$ the morphism to $T$ of step 4 and thus a morphism $U_V\to Y$ over $X$. The two maps on $U_V\times_UU_V$ agree precisely because the descent datum in step 5 was obtained from this sheaf's restrictions. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] they glue uniquely to $U\to Y$; the structural equality over $X$ also descends uniquely. Conversely an $X$-map $U\to Y$ pulls back to a map to $T$, hence a lattice section on $U_V$; its compatibility gives a unique section on $U$ by the sheaf property proved in step 2. The constructions are inverse after the covering and therefore globally, and commute with pullbacks in $U$. Thus $Y$ represents $\mathcal{L}\mathit{at}$; define $\mathrm{Lat}(L)=Y$.

source.place: (2), identify the descended scheme with the original sheaf

proof.text: By [det-pe-morphisms-etale-comparison], $q:Y\to X$ is weakly étale, so $Y$ is itself an object of the pro-étale site (in the containing universe fixed in the statement). Evaluate the representing isomorphism of step 8 on $\mathrm{id}_Y\in\operatorname{Hom}_X(Y,Y)$. This gives a section of $\mathcal{L}\mathit{at}(Y)$, namely a lisse embedded lattice $M^{\mathrm{univ}}\subseteq L|_Y=q^*L$ with $M^{\mathrm{univ}}[1/\ell]=q^*L$. Naturality says that every $f:U\to Y$ pulls it back to the section classified by $f$, which is the universal property. On the component of $T$ labelled by $g\operatorname{GL}_r(A)$ its restriction is $gA_V^r$, so this is also the lattice described in the source's local construction. This proves clause (3).

source.place: (3), universal lattice by the representing section

proof.text: The set $S$ is nonempty for every $r\geq0$, including $r=0$, where it is a singleton and the unique lattice is zero; the construction then gives $Y=X$. If $X$ is empty its site has only empty objects up to isomorphism and its lattice sheaf is terminal, represented by the empty $X$-scheme with the zero universal module. This also follows by using the empty trivializing family throughout. No positive-rank, nonempty-base or Noetherian hypothesis was introduced.

proof_origin.place: (1)–(3), with explicit ind-quasi-affine descent and representing universal section; local classification follows Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.8.4(6)

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NF-dadb68c76 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full: the statement and all 10 steps, against the main-20261015 blueprint statement and proof (1)-(3), the unit sk-lem-stratified-lattice, and Stacks 0APK/0AP6. The statement is the blueprint's verbatim, with the chapter conventions made explicit; nothing is weakened. No new nodes. Every cited statement says what its step uses. Step 1: totally disconnected comparison plus A[1/l]=E with flatness, so M[1/l]=L iff E⊗M→L is an iso. Step 2: pair↔embedded-lattice bijection reduces clause (1) to lem-weil-pbc-lattice-sheaf-locally-constant. Step 3: the finite affine pro-étale chart p is flat, surjective, quasi-compact (X is quasi-separated) and an fpqc cover. Steps 4-5: clopen labels via 03YW(b) give T representing the constant sheaf and a scheme descent datum, with no continuity gap. Steps 7-9: étale and separated descend by 02VN/02KU, representability follows from 023Q, and M^univ is obtained by evaluating at id_Y. Edge cases r=0, X empty and r=1 (torsor, not quasi-compact) are consistent. No cycle, no duplicate: lem-weil-pbc-continuous-etale-local-lattice is Noetherian-only and asserts no representability. FIX (E1, minor): step 6 checked the 0APK node's hypothesis but omitted quasi-compactness of K∩(finite union of copies of B'), which def-nagata quasi-affine requires. I added it with [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs].
